Title: Avery’s Gift
Content: “Everything looks beautiful,” Avery whispered to Danielle as they waited for others to arrive. Balloons and flowers festooned the music room, and above the table lavishly laden with cookies and punch stretched a banner that read, “Happy retirement, Mrs. Vadakin! We’ll miss you!”

But as perfect as everything looked, Avery couldn’t help feeling beset by doubts. More students began to arrive, and teachers and parents, and a mass of cards and gifts began to grow on the table next to the food. Avery held onto the large manila envelope she’d brought, a viper in her hand, `ultext(agitated)` by thoughts that she should have gotten Mrs. Vadakin something else.
“What’s in the envelope anyway?” asked Danielle, nibbling a cookie.
Avery, embarrassed, replied, “It’s something I wrote for Mrs. Vadakin.”
Avery lowered her voice. “Not an essay, a piece of piano music.”
“A composition?” Danielle asked. “I didn’t know you composed!”

Avery looked at the envelope in her hands, hoping it hadn’t been a mistake, hoping it wasn’t too ridiculous a gift for an exceptional teacher. Avery didn’t actually write music, but her father was a professional composer, creating masterpieces for both film and theater. He was the `text(one)` who convinced her to try, arguing an original arrangement was the perfect gift — something meaningful.

So, her father transcribed the piece for her. Note by note, chord by chord, Avery played her piece repeatedly while he wrote out the notes, and when they finished several `text(hours)` later, Avery was flushed with accomplishment.
But now the reservations had returned. Reluctantly, Avery sidled up to the table and began to slip her envelope into the mound.
Danielle snatched it up, and to Avery’s mortification, called out “Mrs. Vadakin, Avery has a unique gift for you!”
Avery froze while Mrs. Vadakin took the envelope and opened it, her mouth dropping open in surprise.
“May I play this right now?” Avery closed her eyes and wished herself a `text(thousand miles)` away as Mrs. Vadakin moved to the piano and settled herself at the bench and everyone gathered.

While Mrs. Vadakin played, Avery’s melody, full of light and shadows, filled the room. When the final haunting chord hung in the air, everyone burst into applause. Avery blushed but smiled back at Mrs. Vadakin, whose eyes glistened with tears.
Her father was right: this was the perfect gift.
